subject: HIPAA / BAA eligibility - post-demo follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@medhealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-20T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: HIPAA / BAA eligibility - post-demo follow-up

Hi Alex - great speaking with you and Priya earlier. Quick recap from our call and next steps so your InfoSec and legal teams have what they need:

- Summary: MedHealth is evaluating Redwood for clinical QA workflows that will touch PHI.
- HIPAA / BAA: Redwood can execute a BAA, but availability depends on deployment mode. See details below.
- SOC 2: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II (audit report available on request) - we can share the report under an NDA/secure upload.

PHI handling & eligible deployment modes (high level):
- Hosted (public Redwood API): NOT eligible for PHI or covered data.
- Dedicated (customer-dedicated GPU pools): Eligible for PHI with a signed BAA; data isolation and retention policies configurable.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): Eligible for PHI with a signed BAA; customer-managed networking and optional on-prem package for stricter controls.

Next steps I propose:
1) I attached a short HIPAA FAQ and our standard BAA draft for initial review (Redwood-BAA-draft.pdf).
2) Please send over your vendor security questionnaire (we can fill and return) - I noticed Priya was going to share the XLS.
3) If helpful, schedule a follow-up with our security/infra lead (Vivek) and legal to go over config and timelines.

Action items for MedHealth: share vendor questionnaire + any specific regulatory requirements (e.g., data residency, logging/audit scope).

I left some notes on likely timelines: Dedicated setup is typically 2-4 weeks once procurement and legal are complete; Private VPC/on-prem can be 4-8 weeks depending on network and install windows. I can give a more detailed runbook after we review the questionnaire.

Attachments: HIPAA-FAQ.pdf, Redwood-BAA-draft.pdf

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Thanks Marissa - really useful summary. A couple quick clarifications from our side:

- Can you confirm that Hosted (public API) is entirely off-limits for any PHI? Our product team wants to be explicit.
- Will the BAA cover both Dedicated and Private deployments identically, or are there differences we should expect?
- Can you share the SOC 2 Type II report or an executive summary? We will route that to InfoSec.

Also attaching our vendor questionnaire (MedHealth_Vendor_Q.xls) for your security team to complete. Ideally we'd get the questionnaire back within 5 business days so we can continue procurement.

Appreciate a point-by-point response we can include in our vendor evaluation.

Best,
Alex
Head of Partnerships | MedHealth Analytics
alex.johnson@medhealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: HIPAA / BAA eligibility - post-demo follow-up

Hi Alex - thanks for sending the questionnaire. Answers below in-line to help you paste into your evaluation doc, plus next steps.

1) Hosted (public API): Confirmed - the Hosted public API is NOT suitable for PHI. We intentionally disallow storing or processing PHI on that tier. Any request that might include PHI should be routed to Dedicated or Private.

2) BAA coverage: Our standard BAA is available for Dedicated and Private deployments. The commercial terms are the same, but implementation specifics (e.g., logging endpoints, key management) differ slightly:
- Dedicated: Redwood provisions customer-dedicated GPU pools in our environment; we manage compute but provide data isolation, configurable retention, and KMS integrations.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): Customer manages networking; optional on-prem package removes our direct network access. BAA language is substantially similar; we include addenda for on-prem and cross-account key handling when applicable.

3) SOC 2: We have SOC 2 Type II (rolled-up report for our platform). We can share the SOC 2 redacted report via secure upload or under NDA. I've copied Vivek (security/infra) to coordinate the transfer.

4) Vendor questionnaire: Neha will take point on the questionnaire and return the completed XLS within 3 business days. If your questionnaire needs specific config examples (VPC peering, subnets, audit log retention), please flag which sections are highest priority and Neha will prioritize.

5) Proposed next steps:
- I will upload the BAA draft to a secure link and share DocuSign once legal approves (link below).
- Schedule a 30-minute call with Vivek + our legal to walk through any contract redlines.

Links / attachments:
- Redwood BAA draft: https://redwood-inference.app/secure/BAA-draft
- DocuSign (placeholder): https://docusign.com/sandbox/packet/abc123
- Attachment: Redwood-BAA-draft.pdf

Vivek / Neha - can you confirm when you can pick this up?

Thanks,
Marissa
